title: The Stokes resistance of an arbitrary particle: a classification of hydrodynamic symmetries
summary: The linearity of the Stokes equations organises the hydrodynamic response of a rigid particle into a hierarchy of resistance operators, coupling successive truncations of the ambient-flow jet to moments of the surface traction. Since the work of Kelvin and Larmor, it has been known that this response does not resolve particle geometry faithfully: bodies with discrete rotational symmetry may be indistinguishable from bodies of revolution (Brenner's helicoidal symmetry) and a chiral body may respond isotropically, as in Kelvin's isotropic helicoid.
